To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tomato plants exposed to the whitefly vector carrying PepGMV ( Begomoviruses, Geminivirdae ) exhibited differential expression of a large number of genes that are associated with the plant defense response.

tomato plants exposed to virulent whitefly feeding (compared to nonvirulent whitefly feeding and noninoculated negative controls) exhibit significant differences in gene expressions, which are associated with defense, pathogen, photosynthesis, and signal transduction-related responses.

tomato plants exposed to virulent and avirulent whitefly feeding exhibited differentially expressed genes that are involved in defense and stress responses, photosynthesis, pathogenesis, and signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of plant responses to whitefly feeding, and the identification of genes involved in the defense response of tomato plants to whitefly feeding and the virus that they transmit.
understanding the molecular basis of plant–insect interactions and plant defense responses to insect feeding and virus infection.
the identification and characterization of genes that are differentially expressed in response to the feeding of nonviruliferously and viruliferously whiteflies on tomato.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
whiteflies and their associated viruses have the potential to induce a broad range of plant defense responses that can be detected by microarray analysis.
the whitefly feeding on the tomato plants induced a significant number of genes that were associated with plant stress and defense responses.

whitefly feeding and virus infection induced differentially regulated genes in tomato plants, and these genes are associated with the major physiological functions that include defense-, pathogen-related, photosynthesis-, and other signaling-related responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
whitefly feeding and virus infection induced the expression of genes that are associated with plant defense responses and pathogenesis.

the viruliferous feeding of whiteflies, in contrast to nonvirulifierous feeding, resulted in the induction of a wide range of plant defense responses that included the expression of genes encoding proteins involved in the synthesis of secondary metabolites, pathogen resistance proteins, and protease inhibitors, as well as genes involved in the regulation of plant defense responses.

tomato plants inoculated with viruliferous (virus carrying) whiteflies exhibited significantly more gene expression changes than plants fed upon by nonvirulferous whiteflies or nonwounded control plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of a large array of genes is differentially regulated in tomato plants exposed to the nonviruliferus or viruliferous feeding of the whitefly vector harboring the geminiviral pathogen PepGMV.
the expression of a large array of genes in tomato plants is significantly altered by the exposure of tomato plants to the whitefly vector carrying a virus.

the microarray analysis yielded an array of genes, which were differentially expressed, in tomato plants 2 weeks after they were exposed, by feeding by nonvirulent whitefly or by whiteflies carrying PepGMV (Begomovirus, Gemiviridae).
